subject: Governed pilot acceptance and safety checks
messages:
From: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
To: samir@acme.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 10 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Governed pilot acceptance and safety checks

Hi Samir —

Great talking yesterday. Per our discussion I've put together a single-page mutual action plan that focuses on the concrete acceptance tests and exit gates we want to use for the 4-week pilot. The purpose here is to make the decision at the end of the pilot objective and operationally verifiable (not just a high-level feeling).

Key asks in this email: please review the acceptance tests in the attached MAP, flag anything you think is missing, and confirm procurement contact who will own the contract milestone for week 4.

High-level summary (from the doc):
- Pilot length: 4 weeks (start target: 2025-11-24)
- Decision points: Week 2 smoke test (go/no-go for continued tuning) and Week 4 executive sign-off
- Lead owners: Acme - Samir (product), Redwood - Jasmine (CS lead), Redwood SE - Karthik

Examples of acceptance tests included (full list in attachment):
- Functional accuracy: classification F1 >= 0.90 on the agreed 1k-sample test set (stratified across departments)
- Embedding recall: mean reciprocal rank >= 0.75 for top-5 retrieval tasks against Acme seed corpus
- Latency: P95 end-to-end inference < 300ms for 512-token requests under realistic traffic profile
- Cost: average inference cost <= $1.80 per 1k tokens with Redwood batching profile applied
- Stability: runtime error rate < 0.5% across all API calls during pilot window
- Security/compliance: SOC2 report + evidence checklist items delivered by Redwood by Week 1

Attachments: redwood_map_v1.docx (MAP with test owners and schedule) and eval_test_suite.csv (test harness, sample queries).

If that looks good I'll push a version into the shared Drive and we can lock milestones with procurement.

Thanks —
Jasmine Liu
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
Attach: redwood_map_v1.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document, 42KB)
Attach: eval_test_suite.csv (text/csv, 18KB)

Jasmine —

Thanks for sending. Glance-through feedback: overall this looks sensible and I like how the MAP ties metrics to concrete artifacts. A few clarifying items from our side before we lock: 

1) Can you call out the exact seed dataset we'll use for the F1 test? We need to confirm sensitive PII handling and whether synthetic masking is applied.
2) For the embedding MRR test, can you include the exact retrieval pipeline (embedding model + vector DB config)? We run everything in our VPC so details matter.
3) Latency target looks fine but we need an explicit note about test load shape — can Week 2 smoke simulate 10 rps sustained for 5 minutes?
4) Procurement: please add the clause that final payment is tied to Week 4 "acceptance sign-off" and that DocuSign will be used.

I cc'd procurement so they can intercept the contract stuff. I'll loop in our infra lead if we need to set up VPC peering.

Samir
Director of Product
Acme AI

Looping in Ben and putting preliminary SE responses inline to Samir's questions. I'm proposing explicit pass/fail thresholds so the MAP is binary at each gate. Below are suggested clarifications we should add to redwood_map_v1.docx before we send final: 

1) Dataset definition and PII handling:
- Test set: 1,000 de-identified rows provided by Acme (stratified by use case). Redwood to run local masking if raw PII present; hashed IDs only stored.
- Evidence: commit of de-id script and sample transformed rows delivered to Acme drive by Day 3.

2) Embedding retrieval pipeline (for MRR test):
- Embedding model: redwood-embed-4k-v1 (or compatible)
- Vector store: Acme-managed Pinecone index (namespace: acme_pilot_2025)
- Similarity metric: cosine; MRR >= 0.75 for top-5 across 200 sample queries

3) Load profile and latency measurement: 
- Smoke test (Week 2): run 10 RPS sustained for a rolling 5-minute window; measure P95 end-to-end including network and client-side transform
- Acceptance (Week 4): measure P95 on a 30-minute synthetic traffic window reflecting production percentiles (sampled from Acme production histogram)
- P95 target: < 300ms for 512-token requests when using Redwood's continuous batching; if pilot uses private deployment, target adjusts to < 220ms

4) Cost accounting: 
- Use Redwood billing snapshot for pilot; target average <= $1.80 per 1k tokens. If average exceeds target by >25% for two consecutive days, map triggers a remediation sprint and temporary cost cap.

5) Quality tests (functional accuracy):
- Classification: F1 >= 0.90 on stratified set; test harness seeds are in eval_test_suite.csv. Pass only if both macro-F1 >= 0.90 and no subgroup < 0.82.
- Regression rules: any drop in F1 > 0.03 from baseline triggers rollback to previous model variant.

6) Security/compliance evidence:
- Redwood provides SOC2 summary + audit artifact list by Day 2; full SOC2 package by Day 7.

Ben: can you confirm the exact names of the test scripts and owners? I'll fold this into the map and send back to Samir.

—Karthik
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
